cpp_findings.citation: CMake provides direct integration with CTest via the enable_testing() and add_test() commands.
cpp_findings.point: Dimension 1 (native test-runner integration): CMake ships CTest as part of the same suite, wired in with two commands.

cpp_findings.citation: CTest integrates well with all major testing frameworks, such as google test (gtest), but if you can't be bothered, just write a simple C++ source file with a single main() function
cpp_findings.point: CTest is framework-agnostic and integrates well with popular unit-test frameworks, or plain assert-based executables.

cpp_findings.citation: This option allows CTest to resume a test set execution that was previously interrupted.
cpp_findings.point: Dimension 3 (advanced execution features): parallel job-server integration, resumable/failover runs, and randomized ordering to catch implicit test-order dependencies are built into ctest(1).

cpp_findings.citation: CTest also has advanced mechanisms for scripting, fixtures, sanitizers, job servers, metric reportings, and much more.
cpp_findings.point: CTest also supports fixtures, sanitizers, job servers and metric reporting beyond the basic pass/fail model.

command for testing CMake projects.
cpp_findings.point: Dimension 2 (CI integration): dedicated, actively used GitHub Actions marketplace actions wrap ctest directly for CI pipelines.

cpp_findings.citation: Include this module in the top CMakeLists.txt file of a project to enable testing with CTest and dashboard submissions to CDash
cpp_findings.point: Dimension 2 continued: CMake/CTest also has first-class dashboard submission support via CDash, separate from generic CI.

cpp_findings.citation: This integration enables users to: Discover tests defined in CMake projects via CTest.
cpp_findings.point: IDE integration: VS Code's official CMake Tools extension provides deep, structured integration between CTest and the editor's native Test Explorer, including result parsing and coverage.

cpp_findings.citation: Both integrate seamlessly with CMake and handle the complex task of building C++ libraries with correct compiler flags, architectures, and linkage options.
cpp_findings.point: Dimension 4 (coherence penalty): package managers (vcpkg, Conan) are separate tools from the build/test system and require explicit toolchain-file or generator wiring into CMake rather than being unified out of the box.

rubric.description: Frozen 0-100 rubric applied identically to all 10 languages (this shard scores only C++; other language shards score the remaining languages against the same rubric so the runner can merge disjoint keys). Score is a qualitative composite of four equally-weighted dimensions, each 0-25 points: (1) existence of a de-facto-standard build tool with native/first-class test-runner integration (not a bolted-on third-party wrapper); (2) breadth/turnkey-ness of CI system integration (official or widely-used marketplace actions, dashboard/report submission); (3) advanced test-execution feature depth (parallel execution, filtering/regex selection, fixtures, coverage hooks, resumability, randomized ordering, sanitizer integration); (4) coherence/unification of the build+test+dependency story (single dominant toolchain vs. fragmented competing tools requiring manual glue).

metric.build_test_integration.score_derivation: Dimension 1: 24/25 (CTest is the mature, native, de-facto-standard test runner shipped with CMake, the dominant C++ build system). Dimension 2: 23/25 (turnkey GitHub Actions support plus CDash dashboards; slightly behind languages with a single official first-party CI-integrated test command). Dimension 3: 23/25 (parallelism, fixtures, sanitizers, resumability, randomized ordering all present). Dimension 4: 17/25 (build system, test runner and package manager are three separately maintained projects needing manual glue, unlike languages with one unified toolchain command). Total = 87/100.

cpp_findings.citation: a more convenient version of the C and C++ standards
cpp_findings.point: cppreference.com is the community's de-facto complete reference for the language and standard library, explicitly designed to substitute for a plain reading of the ISO standard text.

cpp_findings.citation: C++23 is the most recently published C++ Standard (and C++26 is on the way), so that is the main focus of this site.
cpp_findings.point: Dimension 2 (currency): the site actively documents the latest published standard plus in-progress drafts of the next one.

cpp_findings.citation: Also see cppreference.com, which is not authoritative but also can be used for general unofficial reference to answer basic questions about C++.
cpp_findings.point: cppreference explicitly is not the authoritative source; the ISO committee's own portal states it is unofficial.

Dimension 3 (spec + best practices): the formal ISO standard requires purchase, and the official isocpp.org site instead redirects learners to third-party books and the community-maintained C++ Core Guidelines.

cpp_findings.citation: C++ Core Guidelines — By Bjarne Stroustrup and Herb Sutter.
cpp_findings.point: The C++ Core Guidelines provide curated best-practice documentation, authored by the language's original designer and a standards leader.

cpp_findings.citation: GNU libstdc++ — Reference manual for the GNU implementation of the C++ library.
cpp_findings.point: Dimension 4 (fragmentation penalty): the standard library has multiple divergent implementation-specific reference manuals (MSVC, GNU libstdc++, LLVM libc++, plus historical Dinkumware/SGI docs) that cppreference's own resource page lists as separate authorities a developer may need to consult.

rubric.description: Frozen 0-100 rubric applied identically to all 10 languages. Four equally-weighted dimensions, each 0-25 points: (1) existence and completeness of an authoritative or de-facto-standard reference covering the full language plus standard library; (2) currency -- documentation actively tracks the latest language/standard version and drafts of the next one; (3) availability of the formal specification text and curated best-practice/style guidance; (4) coherence -- a single unified official documentation portal vs. fragmentation across multiple non-canonical or implementation-specific references that a learner must reconcile.

metric.documentation_quality.score_derivation: Dimension 1: 23/25 (cppreference is comprehensive and effectively the standard community reference, but is explicitly a non-authoritative substitute for the real standard). Dimension 2: 22/25 (kept current with newest and draft standards). Dimension 3: 17/25 (formal standard text is paywalled -- unlike languages with a free official spec -- though the Core Guidelines partially compensate). Dimension 4: 20/25 (fragmentation across libstdc++/libc++/MSVC-STL/cplusplus.com references, no single official government-of-truth portal analogous to some other languages' unified official doc sites). Total = 82/100.
